subject.title: [Bug]: Potential resource leak in runBoundTurnWithMissingThreadRecovery -- retry not wrapped in try/finally after thread spawn

question: Should Codex app-server bound conversation threads keep a persistent subscription across turns, or should OpenClaw reattach before each bound turn and unsubscribe after every turn including failed recovery retries?
rationale: Both source and Codex contract evidence show that cleanup is possible, but changing subscription ownership can either leak loaded threads or break later bound-turn notifications unless maintainers choose the lifecycle contract.

options.title: Reattach before each turn
options.body: Make bound turns explicitly reattach or resume before turn/start, then unsubscribe in all terminal paths including recovery retry failure, with two-consecutive-turn coverage.

options.title: Keep persistent subscriptions
options.body: Treat the current persistent subscription as intentional for conversation bindings and limit the issue to documentation or observability around loaded thread lifetime.

options.title: Clear failed replacement binding
options.body: On replacement retry failure, clear the saved binding so the next inbound creates a fresh subscribed thread, accepting loss of continuity after that failure.

recommendation.title: Reattach before each turn
recommendation.body: Make bound turns explicitly reattach or resume before turn/start, then unsubscribe in all terminal paths including recovery retry failure, with two-consecutive-turn coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the recovery commit as committer and to adjacent app-server lifecycle cleanup work.
